adventures.title: The Fence at Crow Road
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; authority inquiry/crew withdrawal/stand, commissioner wait/public-work completion, combat and injured withdrawal outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The landowners’ men own pasture but not the county verge; waiting for the commissioner, finishing with witnesses, and standing ground remain separate. Crew withdrawal leaves the gap open and workers safe. Combat win reaches commissioner verification; loss preserves workers/tools and withholds the protection bonus. Existing wage-exclusion regression supports but does not replace this route trace.

adventures.title: The Glass-Plate Box
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; blanket/map-case protection, box-first/camera-first crossing, turnback, combat win and loss traced
adventures.notes: Both protective Gear choices require possession and usability. Carrying the plate box first yields intact plates; camera-first and combat loss lead to the cracked-plate outcome, while turning back preserves the plates but delays delivery. Combat victory protects Lyle and does not claim that the Traveler carried either object.

adventures.title: The Night Mail Train
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; sack watch, passenger shelter, parcel-room transfer, porter call, combat and delay outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The direct parcel-room route transfers the sacks with the agent’s key. On the passenger-shelter route, sacks stay in view until the agent returns and records them inside; that subsequent securing action is expressly attributed to the agent. The whistle route brings a porter onto watch, while winning the stop prevents the attempted theft before arrival. Delay and shared-awning results do not claim opened or lost mail.

adventures.title: The Bridge Pins
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; rope-secure, watch/move, crew-clear, thief combat win/loss, beam-clear and partial outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The rope route secures the chest to the cart; the alternate watch-and-move route enters a beam scene that explicitly establishes the chest as secure before either outcome. The partial result’s tied-to-cart wording is consistent with that intervening state. Crew evacuation remains distinct from chest protection; the combat-loss partial still states the resulting near miss without claiming that the workers were cleared by the Traveler.

adventures.title: The Lost Child’s Lantern
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; whistle/wait signal, known-gate route, hidden-ditch retreat/call, lantern-fetch and both-child outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The brother remains at a known post when signaled; gate routes bring both children together, while the lantern route deliberately returns to the farm for a light and leads them by the fence. The ditch route retreats rather than crossing the drop; finding the gate can continue through the farmstead before the described lantern-guided return. Meal/wick and coin/parish outcomes remain tied to the distinct endings.

adventures.title: The Telegraph Repair Car
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; marker/gloves/mirror availability, closure, wave/handcar block, tester/firm-pole repair and climb/brace outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The local choice helper adds usableItems to every named item requirement, including marker, gloves, mirror and tester. The tester variant claims continuity but explicitly not pole safety; second-pole relay, line closure and direct bracing remain distinct. Waving and blocking with the handcar lead to the appropriate safe and damage outcomes.

adventures.title: The Supper Wagon
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; cook-supplied cover, rest/delay, usable whistle, hand-carry, horse return and hammer-clearing outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The blanket is supplied by the cook; the Traveler’s Farm Whistle is possession-and-usability gated by the helper. Carrying food while the team rests, returning the horse for camp collection, and shifting the branch with a usable hammer lead to separate route results and fees.

adventures.title: The Fence at the Fog Line
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; usable marker/rope, long/short boardwalk, wait, porter-slip and jar-movement outcomes traced
adventures.notes: Marker and rope actions are possession-and-usability gated. The intact long boardwalk is late but safe; the missing-plank crossing has a shaken porter. Helping the slipping porter before moving the jar remains distinct from asking Kersey to move it while the Traveler helps.

adventures.title: The Lumber Crew at the Gully
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; owned stretcher, crew loan, line rescue, saw-first, slow/alone lift and item transfer traced
adventures.notes: The crew-loan route is the only rescue path that begins without the Traveler’s own stretcher and permits accepting the retired spare; the owned-stretcher route excludes that grant. Rope rescue and saw-first preserve the worker/saw priority distinction. The conditional ownership sentence is supported only when the acceptance effect occurs; strain and delay remain explicit.

adventures.title: The Quiet Coffin Cart
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; usable rope/wedge brake methods, turnback, family steadying, unload/carry and fee traced
adventures.notes: Both named Gear methods require usable equipment. Turning back delays the service without risking the coffin; after braking, the family either steadies the cart or unloads and carries it uphill. Only the narrated arrival route pays the stated two-coin fee.

adventures.title: The Silent Warehouse Shift
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; list/lantern/watch, crate-first, worker-first, combat success/loss, ember and pursuit outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The two evacuation actions set distinct history flags and the ending chooses the corresponding order-specific text; both keep oil sealed and people clear. Combat success stops the attempted theft before the figure leaves and reaches evacuation; loss takes the figure out the river door while goods remain safe and no pursuit bonus is paid. Watch/help and fight outcomes preserve the different crate-handling claims.

adventures.title: The Last Mile of the Medicine Wagon
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; bridge/side-path/load/test branches traced
adventures.notes: The sounding-rod route ends by saying a farm cart takes the medicine by the lower road, but only the separate wagon -> load branch introduces a farm cart and its transfer choice. The worker-first side path can send medicine by another cart, but the rod-test branch contains no cart contact or transfer. Other routes distinguish worker rescue, delayed medicine, transfer, driver custody, and delivery wage.

adventures.title: The Watch at the Sheepfold
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; fold/approach/response/creek/dawn branches traced
adventures.notes: The stay/lamp -> approach.lamb route reaches safe without hearing the answering whistle or meeting the neighbor, yet safe says the neighbor secures a loose ewe. The answer -> response branch establishes the neighbor and loose ewe; creek and dawn outcomes retain their separate animal/waiting results. Named Gear requirements include usability.

adventures.title: The Broken Axle Relay
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; driver-care, axle-load, delegation, split-arrival and wait outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The Folding Carriage Jack choice is produced with both items and usableItems requirements by the source choice helper, so BROKEN Gear cannot satisfy it. Driver-first care, loaded axle/teamster assistance, delegation, and second-cart delay outcomes distinguish axle delivery, driver care, and wage effects.

adventures.title: The Second Brace
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; measuring, plumb, square, unsafe-fit, repair and share outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The measure choice checks only inventory ownership of the Joiner’s Folding Rule, sets checked_diagonals, and proceeds as if both diagonals were measured. BROKEN Gear remains in inventory and passes items-only requirements; the parallel Brass Plumb Bob use explicitly requires usableItems. Repair variants, unsafe brace, and wage/tool/Knowledge/declined shares are route-specific.

adventures.title: A Rim before Rain
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; spoke inspection, wrench-assisted inspection, replacement, delay and unsafe-wedge outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The Compact Wheel Wrench option requires usability. Replacing the split spoke or explicitly delaying for a proper spoke both converge only after the crack is demonstrated and wheel work is completed or deferred; driving the wedge early reaches the separate failure result. Wage/tool/Knowledge choices remain distinct.

adventures.title: The Iron That Went Blue
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; inspect/bellows, redraw, pin-and-return, unsafe-strike and share outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The temporary wooden pin route explicitly says Miriam cuts away weakened iron and draws a new eye before the Traveler returns; the shared hinge-settlement claim is established by NPC follow-through rather than falsely attributed to the Traveler. Early-strike failure remains separate.

adventures.title: The Harness Stitch
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; flex/punch, replace/reinforce and unsafe-reuse outcomes traced
adventures.notes: Both diagnostic routes reveal separated inner plies. Replacement explicitly reduces the load; reinforcement explicitly sends one wagon at a time, so the shared slower-trip settlement is supported. Unsafe surface-oiling reaches a separate strap-failure outcome; the reusable lesson is limited to the reinforce action.

adventures.title: The Lantern on the Lower Hook
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; carry-test, replacement/reshaping, shipment refusal and share outcomes traced
adventures.notes: Both reshape and spare-guard replacement routes reach a tested guard that clears the chimney and no longer taps the glass; the ship-first route returns separately and delays handoff before repair. The Lantern Guard field-test choice requires a usable item; share choices remain explicit.

adventures.title: The Roofline in Wind
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; rope/yard-clear, brace/wait, climb/fall and share outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The Travel Rope climb support requires usability. Both safe branches retain ladder/yard precautions; the wait route explicitly waits for calmer weather before Tamsin’s sound-rafter repair and reopening. Climbing to hold the failing gutter reaches a distinct fall/stop-work ending.

adventures.title: The Line That Would Not Hold
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; splice inspection/tool/tester, repair/relay, climb hazard and share outcomes traced
adventures.notes: Toolkit and Line Tester actions require usable Gear; the initial climb has a separate shock/call-off outcome. Dry-wrap testing restores the station; the rider relay grants Knowledge and sets the lesson flag so the same method is not duplicated at settlement. Reward/wage/decline choices are distinct.

adventures.title: The Press before Noon
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; margin comparison, clean/retest, short correction, spoiled-stack, and reward outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The Joiner’s Folding Rule choice gates only on inventory membership even though it physically compares margins. A BROKEN rule remains owned and can satisfy the choice. The shared test scene then diagnoses the press bed; the short-corrected-notice Knowledge grant and duplicate-lesson prevention remain route-specific.

adventures.title: The Ferry Gate Pin
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; inspect/tool, pin support, replacement delay, force failure and shares traced
adventures.notes: The Foreman’s Multi-tool requires usability. Supporting the gate lets Jonas clear and seat the retainer; the alternate branch expressly waits for a replacement pin before the common settled gate result, while forcing the stiff gate reaches a separate hinge-failure outcome.

adventures.title: The Belt at the Mill
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; alignment/tool diagnosis, bearing cleaning, handcart diversion, overload failure and shares traced
adventures.notes: The Pocket Toolkit requires usability. Both safe choices at the gritty bearing identify completion or safe completion after flour diversion; the settlement describes the unloaded test, gradual feed, and safe share. Restarting immediately under load reaches the distinct spill/stop outcome.

adventures.title: The Stone Quoin
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; lane closure/probe, shoring, delayed second mason, unsafe mortar and shares traced
adventures.notes: The sounding rod requires usability. The safe branches establish either shoring/reset or a delayed second-mason reset; premature mortar reaches a distinct failure result in which Della keeps the lane closed and resets safely.

adventures.title: The Last at the Cobbler
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; boot comparisons, patch/replacement, dispute and shares traced
adventures.notes: Both diagnostic choices reach matching pressure marks and Emmett’s admission; patch and replacement are explicit remedies accepted by the customer. The blame-first route stops before repair, does not charge, and schedules daylight inspection. Tool, wage, Knowledge, and decline choices are explicit.

adventures.title: The Ropewalk Splice
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; mark/clamp/load test, relay/delay, rope repair/upgrade, shares and failure traced
adventures.notes: The Iron Rope Clamp requires usability. The failing full-load route stops on a secondary post; safe routes establish resplicing and a gradual test. Repairs/upgrades to the Traveler’s rope use condition/upgrade gates and set distinct run flags and provenance; learned method is not offered twice.

adventures.title: The Door that Swelled
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; gap inspection, usable pry lift, hinge reset, explain/schedule, and planing failure traced
adventures.notes: The explain/schedule choice only explains seasonal swell and schedules a later trim; it has no hinge-reset effect. The shared settlement nonetheless says the hinge holds and the door opens freely. Only the reset choice explicitly resets the hinge and tests the door. Planing without diagnosis reaches a separate failure result.

adventures.title: Paper under the Press
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; spine support/canvas, copy, wait, press failure, and shares traced
adventures.notes: At ink, the wait choice expressly refuses to open the intact gatherings further until the book dries. That route reaches a shared settlement claiming the intact entries were copied. The copy choice is the only action that establishes transcription; volume drying/sewing protection remains plausible on either route.

adventures.title: The Boat Seam in the Yard
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; leveling/cover/launch, leak, cure/cargo transfer, bucket test and shares traced
adventures.notes: The canvas requires usability. Launching early exposes the leak and diverts to a safe cure/transfer decision; either safe choice keeps the skiff ashore until the patch holds a bucket test, while the cargo-transfer option explicitly sends cargo by sound ferry.

adventures.title: The Horse that Wore One Strap
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; fit/gloves, replacement failure, collar refit, teach-only outcome and shares traced
adventures.notes: At load, the teach choice only shows the farmer the fit marks before the next load and sets Knowledge; it does not refit the collar. The shared settlement claims the traces now share the pull after collar refit, with no later load/refit scene. The explicit refit choice does establish that result; replacing the trace without changing fit reaches a separate repeat-wear ending.

adventures.title: The Clock above the Market
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; independent timing test, bell-lever diagnosis, silence/repair, wrong regulator and payment routes traced
adventures.notes: The striking train is isolated before diagnosis; the incorrect regulator choice reaches a separate failure. The silence route keeps the hands running and prevents a crowded-square chime while deferring post-crowd testing, whereas repair explicitly addresses the dragging lever. Wage, Knowledge, and decline remain explicit.

adventures.title: The Drill at Old Number Seven
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; bit withdrawal, usable-glove inspection, fixing-point change, shoring, force failure and shares traced
adventures.notes: Heavy Leather Gloves require usability. The knot/edge diagnosis distinguishes a safer fixing point from adding a second shore before drilling again; settlement summarizes the resulting light test and conditional crew advance. Forcing the bit reaches the separate brace failure.

adventures.title: The Long Measure at Milepost Nine
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; usable chain/lower-stake measurement, stop-block marking, closure, empty-car test and runaway outcome traced
adventures.notes: Both safe correction choices converge on a settlement stating that a stop block catches the empty test car. The mark choice only sets a stop-block mark and records corrected grade; the close choice closes the siding until railway recheck. Neither choice installs a stop block or performs an empty-car test, and no later test scene intervenes. Loading an empty car directly reaches a separate uncontrolled-roll result.

adventures.title: The Door at the Telephone Office
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; lift/tool, hinge diagnosis, refit versus explanation, premature lock replacement and share outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The explain route only shows the clerk why the lock is not faulty, schedules no physical work, and sets a lesson flag; settlement nevertheless says the door closes without lifting and the original lock stays in service. Only the refit route moves the plate into sound wood and refits the lock. Premature replacement reaches a distinct failure.

adventures.title: The Pump between Fields
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; joint inspection, usable-tool access, drain failure, reseat/test, new cup, trough and shares traced
adventures.notes: The Pocket Toolkit requires usability. Both safe valve choices explicitly reseat or replace the cup; the trough test and dry-garden result follow. Opening the drain too soon has a separate flooding result.

adventures.title: The Slate on the Schoolhouse
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; child/ladder safety, rope tie, lath diagnosis, refit/closure and ladder-slip outcomes traced
adventures.notes: The rope choice says to tie the ladder to a sound porch post but checks only items:['travelRope']; a BROKEN Travel Rope remains owned and can satisfy this physical-use gate. The alternate hold route explicitly fails and closes the entrance until a second tie is fitted.

adventures.title: The Glasshouse Lanterns
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; draft inspection, usable-glove access, cap/air-hole repair, record-only choice, warm-pane failure and shares traced
adventures.notes: The record choice records the airflow pattern and grants the lesson but performs no cap turn, air-hole cleaning, or outdoor test. It reaches shared settlement text claiming both lamps burn steadily in open air. The explicit test choice is the route that performs the repair/test; replacing warm glass reaches a separate break-and-cool result.

adventures.title: The Toolbox at Low Water
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; rope/rod/foreman access, ownership evidence, limited recovery/defer, compensation alternatives and provenance traced
adventures.notes: Rope and sounding rod require usability. The foreman or inventory evidence identifies crew property separately from the private chest; limited-recovery wording expressly leaves unauthorized goods, and the bridge crew signs release of its duplicate kit after its numbered kit is accounted for. Fee, accepted kit, refusal and deferral are distinct.

adventures.title: The Roof Under Ash
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; glove boundary, owner line, hook reach, ownership trace, limited recovery, compensation and deferral traced
adventures.notes: The usable glove route handles only cooler near-side fittings; owner authorization excludes apprentice stock, and the hook route stops the roll at the brick sill. The owner explicitly transfers an intact Lantern Guard from closed stock, distinct from the bent guard/scrap and the apprentice’s roll; recovery fee/refusal/defer are separate.

adventures.title: The Siding Spill
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; waybill, usable-wrench stabilization, worker support, limited recovery/defer, combat/resume and compensation traced
adventures.notes: The usable wrench route explicitly leaves the marked case below the bank. The decision/transfer result nevertheless claims the listed equipment has been returned and a separate unlisted rod is released as the county surveyor’s duplicate, while no route after that evidence recovers/returns the marked equipment or establishes the duplicate’s release. Limited recovery and owner-trace variants do not supply that missing transfer witness.

adventures.title: The Camp That Wasn’t Empty
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; call/tracks/glasses, returning survey hand, ownership/recovery, fee/refusal/reward paths inspected
adventures.notes: The released spare Travel Rope is explicitly described as written off as frayed, but the reward adds it without gainItemConditions. engine.ts itemState/itemCondition default missing item state to NORMAL, so the carried reward is represented as sound and usable rather than frayed. Call, tracks, and glasses routes preserve their distinct observations; defer avoids transfer.

adventures.title: The List Behind the Barn Wall
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; list comparison, wedge brace, repair-history witness, square/hook ownership, compensation and defer routes traced
adventures.notes: The square’s old mark is separated from its later sale; the Gate Hook is separately verified as the farmer’s spare before release. Wedge bracing explicitly does not make the wall safe to enter. The fee/refusal and deferred claim retain disputed property.

adventures.title: The Quarry’s Last Lift
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; staged upper-beam block, rod/foreman evidence, frayed-line limit, safe notes recovery, combat win/loss, fee/reward/defer traced
adventures.notes: The opening explicitly stages the block on a stable upper beam, so the first action needs no carried block-and-tackle. The frayed line prevents moving the block; rod and foreman routes establish the ledge/company-property boundary. The sealed notes are recoverable from a safe shelf, and the combat routes do not loot or resolve ownership; win returns to the decision and loss withdraws without transfer.

adventures.title: The Ferry Chest Below the Landing
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; bank-side sounding, rope stabilization, claim detail, owner contact, sealed return, fee/reward/defer traced
adventures.notes: The claimant’s contents detail supports but does not itself transfer the chest; the ferryman contacts the absent deckhand before authorization. The paid route leaves the chest sealed, and the reward route explicitly returns it intact and gifts the deckhand’s spare Farm Whistle after authorization.

adventures.title: What the Storm Left in the Cellar
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; ledger cover, hook access, contract boundary, tenant case custody, future retrieval and compensation paths traced
adventures.notes: The canvas/hook routes protect or expose the public ledger while marking the tenant’s recently occupied room and named tin case as private. The landlord’s salvage share is his own sheet after the tenant returns and retrieves her case; the fee route takes only the public ledger and explicitly leaves the case sealed.

adventures.title: The Charred Signal Post
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; board lift, inventory, maker/repair mark, serial verification, county return and fee paths traced
adventures.notes: The initial county loss record is not treated as identity proof; the serial is verified by the foreman before the spare mirror reward. The found mirror’s county/private marks and the glass worker’s prior sale account are kept distinct; fee returns the found mirror to the crew.

adventures.title: The Pack Frame in the Ravine
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; mule/handler stabilization, rope lift, parcel seal, qualifying recovery gate, fee/refusal/defer traced
adventures.notes: The outfitter replacement is gated on both the rope-lift access flag and limited recovery; the rope route explicitly raises the rented frame while leaving the snagged medicine parcel lower. The other access routes cannot qualify for the replacement. The fee makes no extra recovery claim, and deferral leaves all property with its owner.

adventures.title: The Lantern Crate in the Washout
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; wedge/light/foreman routes, explicit unstable-bank warning, limited recovery, repair/reward/fee/defer traced
adventures.notes: The wedge route says the larger shelf still shifts and must not be entered; the stable-road light route only inspects, and the foreman route marks ownership. Nevertheless, the generic secureRecovery choice advances directly to a decision whose property text says all three serviceable lamps were returned and releases the damaged Roadman’s Lantern, with no stabilization/entry/retrieval step. The damaged-lantern repair/reward and fee/defer paths do not establish safe access to the buried crate.

adventures.title: The Ledger at the Weir
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; bank-side hook, worker-copy issue, clasp/seal, sealed return, duplicate tool, fee/defer traced
adventures.notes: The hook reaches the book from the stone walk; the worker states that copies of names/sums matter, and the outcome asks the clerk to make those copies while keeping the ledger sealed during recovery. The duplicate hook is a separate miller’s crew reward after ledger return; fee and defer remain alternatives.

adventures.title: Iron at Milepost Nine
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; current inventory/stamp, old records, second-mark inspection, farmhand account, county pry return and wedge release traced
adventures.notes: The county confirms the stamped pry tool should be returned, but the three route variants do not establish abandonment or signed county clearance for the unmarked Steel Wedge: the stamp identifies only the pry tool, the old-record route authorizes transfer of that pry tool after inspection, and the underside date explicitly does not settle wedge ownership. The shared property settlement nevertheless says the county authorizes the wedge as abandoned and offers it as the reward.

adventures.title: The Bell Creek Drift
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; gloves/stitch/hook access, two claimant evidence, owner return, spare reward, repair and combat routes traced
adventures.notes: The donated Freightman’s Strap is described as the second driver’s own sound spare. The reward effects nevertheless include repair:true, which sets the new item’s condition to DAMAGED; engine.ts reads the stored condition rather than the sound narrative. The wet/frayed recovered strap is separately arranged for repair and returned to the first driver, while fee/owner paths do not grant the spare.

adventures.title: The Cache Beneath the Snow Fence
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; compass return line, rod hollow-pocket test, call/response, leader/assistant status, sealed reserve, fee/reward/defer and lore traced
adventures.notes: The response route establishes that the expedition is separated rather than gone; the rod route checks the adjacent hollow from firm ground and the compass route records only return bearing. The reserve remains the party’s shared property, with the leader’s recovery and assistant reunion explicitly preceding any duplicate-marker transfer; the fee leaves the bundle sealed and defer avoids the recovery.

adventures.title: The Plates in the Pressroom
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; inventory/type, reimbursement receipt, sealed proof case, personal toolkit claim, owner settlement and fee traced
adventures.notes: The owner’s dated reimbursement receipt settles the printer’s correctly identified toolkit claim, while the type remains office property. The possible libel proof case stays sealed during the former partners’ discussion; duplicate toolkit compensation is separately released from inventory and the fee route leaves tools with their resolved owners.

adventures.title: The Boat on the Gravel Bar
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; wait/keel, shore sounding, ferry line/owner pull, passenger blanket, property return, fee/defer traced
adventures.notes: Waiting exposes the keel without claiming the blanket or ferry line; sounding identifies a far-side drop; the line route steadies the skiff with the owner guiding the pull. The passenger is contacted and explicitly abandons the damaged blanket before the owner’s duplicate pail reward. Fee returns the pail, line and named blanket; defer is not a transfer.

adventures.title: The Heap Behind the Station
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; scrap separation, missing-ledger check, borrower initials, buried gauge, return precondition, owner/fee/combat routes traced
adventures.notes: The railway release is expressly conditioned on returning the borrowed track gauge found beneath the marked wrench. The check/initial routes only establish the wrench’s missing status and borrower; the generic owner-trace path records evidence but effects no gauge return, yet the shared decision still offers the released wrench. The limited-recovery choice does not require or record the gauge handoff either.

adventures.title: The Pack at the Tunnel Mouth
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; call, horse tag, wedge/outside-fall-line pack, owner/crew property, safe recovery, inn/fee/defer traced
adventures.notes: Every route keeps the Traveler outside the unsafe rubble; the wedge route explicitly retrieves only the pack outside the fall line. The horse tag and pack list identify the surveyor, and the loaned roll is distinguished from the surveyor’s own chain before crew accounting and spare transfer. The owner/fee and defer routes do not claim tunnel entry.

adventures.title: The Find Along the Fence Line
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; repair history, maker stamp/work order, boundary-safe mark, custodian and joint permission routes traced
adventures.notes: The disputed boundary does not determine tool ownership; the work order and saddler identify the custodian. The mark-and-avoid route leaves the roll untouched until the saddler arrives, while the later sale follows his abandonment record and both landholders’ access permission. Fee leaves the item with its custodian.

adventures.title: Glass from the Gutter
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; gloves, estate-sheet cover, drainage-hook movement, overhead-frame boundary, cloak ownership and compensation variants traced
adventures.notes: The shared evidence setup says the seed trays are covered before the three route-specific consequences. Only spreading the estate sheet establishes that cover; gloves merely protect hands and the hook only moves loose fragments. Those other routes therefore receive the false covered-tray state and can reach the shared reward text thanking the Traveler for preserving the seed beds.

adventures.title: The Lamp in the Upper Cut
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; safe-line lantern, echo/closed-lower-cut, upper-beam lowering, serial check, loan return, personal spare and fee traced
adventures.notes: The upper lamp can be lowered from the safe ledge; the lower glimmer remains unidentified. The numbered loan lamp is distinguished from the foreman’s personal lantern and return/transfer follows the stated recovery agreement. The fee route explicitly leaves the lower light untouched.

adventures.title: The Chest in the Old Bridge
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; stone-loosening, family contents detail, position record, sealed lift, owner identification and reward/fee traced
adventures.notes: The toolkit loosens surrounding stone only, the chest remains sealed, and the family’s dated description supports identification without opening it. Once lifted, the family opens it with its original key and returns the heirloom square to the county before gifting a duplicate; the fee route delivers the sealed case to family.

adventures.title: The Warehouse After Rain
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; sealed-crate movement, signed return-list/tool ownership, waxed-sheet paper protection, contractor sale, tenant trunk, fee/refusal/defer and cost-gated Gear traced
adventures.notes: Each opening action receives its matching evidence variant. The tool’s contractor mark is followed by the property scene’s explicit former-owner confirmation and one-coin sale; the sealed crates remain sealed and the tenant’s trunk is held unopened. The generated reward requires the coin cost and presents the fee as an alternative; defer/refusal do not transfer Gear.

adventures.title: The Match at the Brace
adventures.reviewProvenance: current-source route review; gradual/full-load test, grain explanation, crack/hold result, award/void/fee variants traced
adventures.notes: The gradual test supports Nell’s safe brace. adventures.title: The Mile Without a Marker

adventures.title: The Cable Ferry in Crosswind

adventures.title: The Boat Hook at the Cattle Bank

adventures.title: The Boat That Came Back Empty

Partial/full compensation and spare flags stay tied to the described warning work.

adventures.title: The Freight Net at Dry Creek

The cargo-first route secures the marked load; using the cargo net as a sole barge mooring is refused.

Reward and delivery text preserve the seal and no forced assistance occurs.

adventures.title: The Wet Manifest at East Wharf

Waiting keeps them there and pays partial work; taking the firm ridge route in groups reaches upper pasture and reunites the drover, while the river ford remains closed. The pack saddle reward does not authorize overloading.

adventures.title: The Cut Wire at Ash Pasture

The replaced repair roll is expressly distinguished from a trace or buckle.

The whistle/coin outcomes are limited to the corresponding completed or partial work.

The refusal route prevents chasing/dispatching Bess; settlement does not claim the dog performed the rescue.

The replaced strap reward is not presented as a recovery tool.

Shouting produces a stop, and rewards do not claim the whistle commands animals.

adventures.title: The Calf with Two Ear Notches

adventures.title: The Saddle Marks on the Wagon

The repair roll does not claim to restore a cracked buckle.

The finish route's high-exit and handler-led stop outcomes remain distinct.

adventures.title: The Calving Lamp at Three Oaks

adventures.title: The Dry Row before the Threshing

The loaded-first routes do have a second-load decision and remain distinct.

adventures.title: The Grain Lift at Low Barn

adventures.title: The Irrigation Stone at South Field

The held-divider branch waits for both owners and the short-flow test does not establish a lasting unilateral right.

The shared reward effect said the Traveler helped move the animals. The separate move option does establish evacuation. Feed-saving and unsafe options are stopped; extinguishing the ember and removing the lantern are otherwise consistent. The C0001 repair now records ember/lantern handling without implying animal movement; route-pair persistence tests pass.

adventures.title: The Hitch Pin at Gray Mill

Feed is unloaded only after the wagon tracks straight; delaying leaves the parked wagon/sacks covered. The reward is a replaced wrench, not a claim that it repaired the pin.

adventures.title: The Night Watch at Hollow Barn

findings.defect: The rescue ending says the road crew came after the Traveler signaled even on the guard-the-cart branch, which performs no signaling action.

findings.defect: An ambiguous address clue is recorded as Knowledge that Nell was intended at the bridge-side door, although the scenario establishes she is staying with her aunt at the mill and the parcel must be carried there to reach her.

findings.violatedRule: Knowledge must distinguish a tentative address inference from a confirmed intended-recipient location, especially when the route evidence remains ambiguous.

findings.defect: The final choice grants History claiming the Traveler spent Christmas night helping delayed passengers at the station on routes where they left or did not help.

findings.violatedRule: Persistent History must record only route-established player participation, location, and actions; completion of a common finale is not proof that every player did the same work.

No new state, persistence, rewards, or other root-cause behavior changed.

Production build and TypeScript pass.

findings.defect: Keeping the letter sealed on the direct mill-delivery route grants Knowledge that it was not an emergency warning without any source establishing its contents or urgency.

findings.defect: The shared settlement and ending claim the miller’s logs were returned even when the player chooses to accept only the neighbor’s own wood and performs no return action.

findings.defect: Calling the driver to abandon the wagon is treated as proof that he reached shore, producing a rescue claim without a completed crossing.
findings.routeWitness: span.reachChild success -> childAcross (text says father still on bridge) -> callFather -> bridgeAftermath -> bridgeEnd; callFather only calls him to leave but sets bridgePeopleSaved, enabling the ending variant that says driver and daughter reach the west bank. muleSaved.muleCallDriver likewise sets that proof after a call alone.
findings.violatedRule: A rescue/location outcome must be established by an action or explicit transition, not inferred from a warning or call; individual person states must remain distinct.
findings.implementationEvidence: The driver-reaching proof was removed from call-only and unconfirmed crossing routes. Shared wagon/drop and final text now keep the driver's location unconfirmed when route evidence does not establish shore arrival; the daughter's and mule's independently established states remain distinct. disasterRescueBatch.stateAware.test.ts drives child-across then callFather and mule-freed then muleCallDriver, confirming neither grants bridgePeopleSaved nor creates a driver-at-shore ending claim.

findings.defect: The run-alongside route is credited with clearing passengers and station hands from the rails and helping avert a collision although it performs no such intervention.
findings.routeWitness: platform.runAlongside -> platformClear has only a health effect; platformClear says the Traveler kept passengers/station hands away, and trainAftermath.trainReport grants collision-prevention History. trainEnd thanks the Traveler for keeping passengers off the line and says their clear account gave crews time.
findings.violatedRule: Persistent participation/history and shared outcome text may only credit actions established by the selected route.

findings.defect: Unwarned routes converge on an ending that says workers were counted outside although their evacuation was never established.
findings.routeWitness: yard.tellForeman -> foremanActs or yard.inspectValve -> valveSeen -> turnWheel success -> vented / wait routes -> boilerAftermath -> boilerEnd. foremanActs says workers are outside only if warned; none of these paths sets boilerShiftWarned or reaches workersOut, while aftermath/end unconditionally say workers are counted outside.
findings.violatedRule: A shared emergency outcome cannot assert people reached safety without route proof; warning, accounting, and evacuation are distinct events.
findings.implementationEvidence: boilerAftermath and boilerEnd no longer claim that workers were counted outside; warning, feed shutdown, pressure relief, and actual evacuation are not conflated. Reward and equipment choices are unchanged. disasterRescueBatch.stateAware.test.ts drives an unwarned feed-shutdown/vent route and a warned-but-incomplete route, verifying both remain free of the unsupported evacuation claim.

findings.defect: The passive wait-after-failure route grants History that the Traveler helped guide the crowd despite stewards opening the gate and no successful crowd intervention by the player.
findings.routeWitness: platform.climbStand failure -> crowdFall.fallStayWall -> crowdSettles -> crowdReport grants 'helped guide a crowd away from a false alarm'; fallStayWall only waits for the surge to thin, and crowdFall states stewards open the west gate.
findings.violatedRule: Persistent History must not turn an unsuccessful attempt or passive presence into completed participation unless the route establishes a contribution.

findings.defect: The direct wall-bracing route reaches shared text claiming the visible pair are already outside although neither was guided out on that route.
findings.routeWitness: hall.braceNorth -> wallBraced; only hall.eastPair leads to pairOut and sets roofPairSafe. wallBraced unconditionally says the two visible people are already outside before offering beamReach/beamKeepOut.
findings.violatedRule: Shared route text must preserve person location and rescue state established by each incoming branch.

findings.defect: Checking the fallen gate is recorded as moving the cow, causing the ending to report it safe without a rescue or relocation action.
findings.routeWitness: crossroads.checkKitchen -> stoveHazard.stoveSmother -> stoveSafe (cow unresolved) -> safeCow ('Check the fallen gate in the orchard') sets tornadoCowMoved -> tornadoEnd says cow safe if freed or moved.
findings.violatedRule: A person/animal safety result must be supported by an action that actually frees or moves them; inspection is not rescue.

findings.defect: A shared safe ending says the clerk corrected the accusation on exit routes that never contacted or heard from the clerk.
findings.routeWitness: bar.quietKitchen -> backAlley.alleyLeave -> safeEnd and bar.drawFirst success -> gunTurn.gunLeave -> safeEnd; neither path reaches clerk or streetSafe, yet safeEnd says 'The clerk’s account corrects the accusation.'
findings.violatedRule: A shared ending may not claim that an accusation was verified or corrected unless that information was obtained on the selected route.

findings.defect: The ending says the coach party travels east under escort even on routes that never summon town help or receive an escort.
findings.routeWitness: coach.treatPassenger -> passengerHelp.helpStayCoach -> survivors -> stageEnd (also tracksReturn/steadyGuard -> survivors); only rideTown/steadyWarn/helpWarnTown reaches townWarn and sends the constable/doctor. survivors explicitly makes the doctor conditional on sending warning, but stageEnd unconditionally asserts escort.
findings.violatedRule: An ending must not promote local aid or waiting into an external escort/resolution that the route did not establish.

findings.defect: The wait-without-contact route reaches a jailer-return scene that includes a clerk’s review of the charge book, although no clerk or deputy was contacted.
findings.routeWitness: cell.waitJailer -> wait.waitStay -> jailerBack; waitJailer does not call anyone, wait says no officer answered a call despite no call choice, and waitStay only remains until someone arrives. jailerBack nevertheless says the clerk found no entry. Explicit clerk paths use sendDeputy/accountOfficer/waitClerk -> officer.
findings.violatedRule: NPC arrival, records review, and institutional conclusions must be tied to route-established contact or an explicit independent arrival.

findings.defect: The shared settlement asserts both the sale receipt’s twelve-calf count and the holding pasture’s eighteen-cattle count even when the player has inspected neither or only one source.
findings.routeWitness: pasture.inspectBrands -> brands.brandsReport -> settlement directly, with no visit to market or holding; alternatively market.marketReceipt -> settlement omits the holding count, and holding.holdingConfer -> settlement omits the receipt. settlement states both counts and concludes the rancher’s count was six too high.
findings.violatedRule: A resolved ownership/count conclusion must be supported by all material records and must not import evidence from unvisited routes.

findings.defect: The book and settled ending import repayment evidence and a harvest-book agreement on routes that do not retrieve or review the book.
findings.routeWitness: distance.distanceTalk -> book and outside.hallCall -> book do not fetch/read the harvest book, but book states an eight-coin repayment. room.grabGun success -> weaponSafe -> gunDepart -> settled also bypasses the book while settled states a conditional four-coin balance and an accepted harvest-book date.
findings.violatedRule: A scene or ending may not assert documentary findings or negotiated terms unless the selected route establishes that the record was reviewed and the terms were accepted.

findings.defect: History records delivery of family news to the wanted son on a route where the Traveler hands the letter to the deputy instead.
findings.routeWitness: purpose.tellDeputy -> deputy.deputyLetter grants 'carried family news to a wanted traveler without helping him escape'; the letter never reaches canyon/handLetter, the only action setting familyNewsDeliveredToSon.
findings.violatedRule: Persistent History must describe the action actually taken and preserve the distinction between carrying a message and delivering it to its intended recipient.

findings.defect: A retreat route without signaling or guiding the rancher grants History credit for helping the rancher leave the armed dispute.
findings.routeWitness: cover.coverLeave -> retreat; retreat says the owner is safe only if they followed a signal, but coverLeave signals no one. retreat.retreatReport nevertheless grants 'helped a rancher leave an armed debt dispute'. termsOwnerLeave is a separate positive route sharing the same grant.
findings.violatedRule: History participation claims require route evidence of the credited action; leaving the scene or reporting it is not proof that another person left.

findings.defect: The copied-map ending identifies an unexplained mark as a water-gate mark even when the third stone was not examined.
findings.routeWitness: ledger.copyMap -> copied and creek.takeTrackBack -> copied; neither route reaches stone.stoneRecord, the only choice that establishes that the third stone marks an old mill water gate.
findings.violatedRule: An ending may not promote an unexamined clue into a confirmed interpretation; seen/copied evidence is distinct from examined/identified evidence.

findings.defect: The shared discovery asserts the family learned the room’s purpose and returned both the sewing box and letters on routes that establish neither or only one of those outcomes.
findings.routeWitness: house.inspectOpening -> opening.openingBrace -> braced.bracedLeave -> discovery establishes no letter reading or object return; boxFound.boxReturn returns only the box; letters.lettersShare returns letters but does not establish box removal/return.
findings.violatedRule: Shared endings must preserve route-specific information acquisition and object custody; partial discovery/return must not become full resolution.

findings.defect: The ending identifies the island as a former freight landing and says the river covers it again on safe-bank/retreat routes that never reach or inspect the island.
findings.routeWitness: bank.waitWater -> wait.waitTurnBack -> discovery, and bank.readPost -> post.postRecord -> discovery; neither enters island/foundation/tin scenes. The post confirms an earlier channel and skiff rib but does not establish the island foundation was a freight landing or that the water later covers it before evening.
findings.violatedRule: Final route summaries must not resolve locations or later environmental outcomes beyond the evidence and time transitions established on that route.

findings.defect: The discovery attributes the freight-link explanation to the station book and platform chalk even on routes that do not inspect those records.
findings.routeWitness: platform.enterWaiting -> room.roomLeave -> discovery sees only the notice; worker.workerAwning -> awning.awningNotify -> payoff -> discovery obtains the track worker’s account and crate delivery, not the book or chalk. discovery states 'The book and chalk marks explain its use.'
findings.violatedRule: A conclusion should not claim unexamined sources as the route's evidence or imply the player read records they chose not to inspect.

findings.defect: The shared ending supplies the flood-abandonment history and landholder closure action on routes that neither inspect the deed nor contact the landholder.
findings.routeWitness: slope.lookWindow -> room.roomRetreat -> discovery and slope.enterHouse -> upper.upperOut -> discovery; neither route consults landholder or papers, yet discovery states the family left after flood damage and that the landholder will mark the slope closed until shored.
findings.violatedRule: Route convergence must preserve both information provenance and NPC follow-up; one branch's documentary history or contact cannot become universal ending knowledge/action.

findings.defect: The room-only inventory route ends by referring unidentified private letters to the surgeon’s family despite choosing to record blankets and cot only.
findings.routeWitness: gate.readInventory -> plan.planPermission -> permission.openRoom -> room.roomCount -> discovery; roomCount records blankets/cot only, does not identify or return letters, while only room.roomLetters -> records -> fortRecord routes them for family notice.
findings.violatedRule: A shared ending may not claim an institutional or private-property disposition that the selected route did not establish.

findings.defect: Asking the weir keeper what changed immediately grants Knowledge that an injured animal began visiting at dusk, before the account establishes that explanation.
findings.routeWitness: creekSigns.askWeirKeeper grants the injured-animal/track-timing Knowledge before entering weirAccount; weirAccount says only fish are disappearing, one paw print is deeper, and no animal has attacked anyone. Bear confirmation occurs only at creekReveal.
findings.violatedRule: Knowledge must be granted after the selected route establishes the proposition, not as a side effect of asking an unresolved question.

findings.defect: Bear endings and History claim weir closure and farm protection on routes that neither establish closure nor consistently contact the keeper/farm.
findings.routeWitness: shelfTracks.waitAtDistance -> creekReveal.backAwayBear -> bearWithdrawn has no keeper/farm contact but says keeper closes weir and farm moves dogs indoors; creekReveal.rushBear success -> bearDriven likewise has no call yet asserts keeper closure. creekReveal.callKeeperBear only calls the keeper but grants History for helping close the weir before any closure choice/outcome.
findings.violatedRule: NPC follow-up, environmental closure and player participation must be tied to route-established communication and completed action.

findings.defect: Withdrawing to bring a trained crew after locating one miner ends by saying the missing pair are not yet found.
findings.routeWitness: mineMouth.questionForeman -> mineAccount.callIntoShaft -> mineEcho establishes one miner alive in the side chamber; mineEcho.withdrawMine -> mineWaited then says 'The missing pair are not yet found.' The remaining second miner is unresolved, but the first has been located.
findings.violatedRule: Withdrawal may leave part of an objective unresolved, but it must preserve already established person-location and rescue information.

findings.defect: The rope rescue action accepts a BROKEN travel rope because it checks inventory presence rather than usability, then records a successful miner rescue and History credit.
findings.routeWitness: sideChamber.lowerRope requires items:['travelRope'] only and transitions directly to minerOut with 'used rope to rescue a miner'; the engine permits an owned but BROKEN rope to satisfy items without usableItems.
findings.violatedRule: A physically used tool must be usable, not merely present in inventory; broken equipment cannot prove a successful rescue method.
findings.implementationEvidence: Physical Gear-use gates at sideChamber.lowerRope now require usable condition through usableItems/anyUsableItems. The new CRA-C0004 regression matrix verifies normal Gear remains eligible while BROKEN and absent Gear are rejected for this exact route; see src/craC0004GearUsability.test.ts.

findings.defect: The failed brace outcome leaves the second miner trapped but says 'the miners' drag the Traveler toward the air shaft, implying the unresolved miner is present to help.
findings.routeWitness: secondMiner.holdBrace failure message explicitly says the second miner remains behind the brace and advances to mineInjury; mineInjury says the miners drag the Traveler toward the air shaft, while only the first miner was at the shaft and the second remains trapped.
findings.violatedRule: Person presence and participation in an ending must match each individual rescue/location state.

findings.defect: The moundResolved ending claims both the rim is marked and the flock is moved to higher pasture although the markMound route performs only the first action.
findings.routeWitness: westSlope.sheepFreed -> sheepFreed.markMound -> moundResolved; closePasture is the distinct choice leading to flockMoved and is the route that moves the flock.
findings.violatedRule: A converged ending may not attribute an unselected follow-up action to the player/NPC as a completed outcome.

findings.defect: The shared stagAfter ending says the farmer postpones the hunt and livestock are proven responsible on routes that establish neither the farmer's decision nor the crop-loss explanation.
findings.routeWitness: stagAtOrchard.letStagPass/leadFarmerAway and huntersFound.leaveHunters reach stagAfter without farmer agreement or completed evidence; on the hunter route the parties remain arguing, yet the ending says the farmer postpones the hunt and crop loss is traced to livestock.
findings.violatedRule: Shared conclusions and NPC decisions must not exceed the evidence/action established on every incoming route.

findings.defect: The successful strike route reaches campDawn after raising and damaging an exposed lantern, but campDawn says the lantern remains as it is and the presence never touched it while covered.
findings.routeWitness: lightPattern.raiseLantern -> lightApproach (damageItems lantern) -> strikeShape success -> campDawn; the source explicitly damages the exposed lantern before the ending text claims it remained untouched while covered.
findings.violatedRule: Ending text must preserve route-specific object condition and method; exposed/damaged is distinct from covered/untouched.

findings.defect: The direct mark-skiff retreat route claims the helper removes the false light and guides the Traveler to dry ground without encountering or contacting him.
findings.routeWitness: marshEvidence.markSkiff -> marshDeception; only marshHummocks/callForGuide routes establish the ferryman's helper and his assistance, but marshDeception universally says he takes down the light and leads the Traveler out.
findings.violatedRule: A shared ending cannot claim NPC participation or assistance absent route evidence that the NPC was encountered and involved.

findings.defect: The inspect-water choice grants Knowledge identifying a submerged log before the route has probed or otherwise seen the object below the dark water.
findings.routeWitness: riverLanding.inspectWater -> riverCurrent grants 'Small boats were struck by a submerged log'; riverCurrent says the branch is too low to see below dark water; riverEvidence.probeWithPole/probeFromShore is the first route to catch and identify the heavy log.
findings.violatedRule: Knowledge must not promote an observed possibility into a confirmed object/cause before the route establishes it.

findings.defect: The open-culvert choice grants Knowledge that stopping the wheel let the badger leave safely, including on routes where the wheel was not stopped.
findings.routeWitness: millEvidence.setEmptyCrate -> millVisitor.openCulvert and millCadence.watchOneTurn -> millVisitor.openCulvert grant the stopping-wheel conclusion without millCadence.stopWheel; the focused F6 test explicitly verifies watchOneTurn leaves the wheel-turning variant active.
findings.violatedRule: Knowledge about cause/method requires route proof of that method; watching or placing a crate is not stopping the wheel.

findings.defect: The guide-outside route ends with wording that the badger leaves through the culvert, despite the selected route guiding it toward the open yard.
findings.routeWitness: millVisitor.guideOutside -> badgerLeaves; the ending says 'leaves through the culvert' although only openCulvert selects that route and cornerBadger's success explicitly bolts through it.
findings.violatedRule: A shared result must preserve the route-specific exit/location and method rather than narrate one caller's method universally.

findings.defect: The ember-only route reaches an ending that says the trapped worker is safe with the family even though the route never frees the worker from the kiln.
findings.routeWitness: kilnInterior.smotherEmber -> emberStopped; kilnInterior says the worker remains trapped behind a warped door, while emberStopped says 'The worker is safe with the family.' The rescue branches enter kilnRescue first.
findings.violatedRule: A route may not promote partial hazard containment into a completed person-rescue outcome.

findings.defect: The direct retreat-to-bank route can receive Knowledge and shared ending text claiming a tested response to sharp sounds without taking the sound-observation branch.
findings.routeWitness: iceFootsteps.backToNearBank -> iceBank.waitForOthers grants Knowledge and then iceAfter says range/response to sound are known; iceSound is the only scene that explicitly compares boot scrape and buckle sounds, and this direct route never visits it.
findings.violatedRule: Information about an observed causal mechanism must be supported by that route, not borrowed from an alternate branch through shared closure.

findings.defect: Grave closure and miracle-claim routes can assert that a feed tally distinguishes the goats and grant History credit for resolving their identities without visiting the ledger/tally route.
findings.routeWitness: goatMarks.askGravedigger -> goatBurial bypasses goatLedger; goatBurial.closeGrave grants History for resolving identities through the feed tally, while leaveGrave/claimMiracle say the tally distinguishes three goats. Those routes establish ear marks and an empty grave, not the tally.
findings.violatedRule: Knowledge/History about a specific explanation must be granted only when route actions establish that evidence; shared closure cannot import an unvisited record.

findings.defect: The shared widowAfter result claims both fence repair and that the widow stopped leaving food across routes that establish only one or neither action.
findings.routeWitness: stopFeeding reaches widowAfter without neighbor fence repair; repairFence does not establish stop-feeding; leaveDogRoom/closeYardGate/driveDog and mediateFence can also reach widowAfter without those paired outcomes.
findings.violatedRule: Converged outcomes must preserve independently established route actions and must not combine optional interventions universally.

findings.defect: Fetching the keeper from outside the cellar reaches a rescue ending that says the seller reached the yard and the keeper boarded the service opening, without establishing either action.
findings.routeWitness: cellarExterior.fetchKeeper -> cellarRescue bypasses cellarVoice/cellarPassage, hearing the seller, opening/clearing the grate, or entering the passage; cellarRescue then asserts seller-to-yard and keeper-board outcomes.
findings.violatedRule: A route outcome may not claim person movement or completed follow-up actions that the selected path did not establish.
findings.implementationEvidence: The exterior fetch-keeper bypass now ends with the seller's location and any boarding action unconfirmed. Only the explicit cellarPassage.guideSellerOut choice records cellarSellerAtYard and receives the specific rescue variant; failure aftermath no longer invents the seller pulling the Traveler free or the keeper boarding the chute. monsterHuntRc12F6.test.ts covers the bypass, explicit escort, save/reload, and failure route.

findings.defect: The cousin-contact route reaches an ending that asserts the two-brother/exchanged-coat explanation and a human account for the shapeshifter rumor without meeting the tailor who establishes it.
findings.routeWitness: laundryMark.askForCousin -> identityAfter bypasses tailorFound; identityAfter states the towns receive the two-brother/exchanged-coat account. tailorFound is the route establishing the twin explanation; returnedCoachCoat preserves uncertainty in its variant.
findings.violatedRule: An ending and persistent explanation must not promote suspicion or a contact request into confirmed knowledge without the route that establishes the explanation.

findings.defect: The trapResolved result says the dogs return with the trapper on withdrawal and successful den-approach routes where the dogs remain unrecovered.
findings.routeWitness: withdrawDen and successful approachDen reach trapResolved while dogs remain tied/unrecovered; the ending universally states that the dogs return with the trapper.
findings.violatedRule: Outcome summaries must preserve individual person/animal recovery and location state; retreat or partial success is not recovery.

findings.defect: The trapperStopped ending claims the wire is disarmed and the dogs recovered after routes that neither disarm the wire nor establish dog recovery/location.
findings.routeWitness: backTrapperAway/signalTrapperBack reach trapperStopped without the disable/take-chain action; the ending asserts both disarmed wire and recovered dogs despite those state omissions.
findings.violatedRule: A shared outcome cannot imply completed interventions or recovered beings without route proof for each.

findings.defect: The trapLeft ending says the Traveler left before the trapper placed his bedroll even when the player first saw the bedroll already placed and then walked away.
findings.routeWitness: trapperCamp.trapperArgument -> trapperCamp.walkAwayTrap -> trapLeft; trapperArgument establishes the bedroll is already placed, while trapLeft says the Traveler leaves before it is set.
findings.violatedRule: Chronology and object-state narration must reflect the state established before the selected action.

findings.defect: The physical wire-cut action accepts an owned but BROKEN small knife and records a successful cut/free outcome because it checks inventory presence rather than usability.
findings.routeWitness: elkWire.cutWire requires smallKnife in items but not usableItems; an owned BROKEN knife remains present and can transition to the freed-wire result, unlike the rope option's usable-item gate.
findings.violatedRule: A tool used for a physical action must be usable; possession of broken equipment is not proof that the action can be performed.
findings.implementationEvidence: Physical Gear-use gates at elkWire.cutWire now require usable condition through usableItems/anyUsableItems. The new CRA-C0004 regression matrix verifies normal Gear remains eligible while BROKEN and absent Gear are rejected for this exact route; see src/craC0004GearUsability.test.ts.

findings.defect: The shared resolved ending says the disputed sale terms are compared on return-plate/payment routes that do not consult or compare the sale note.
findings.routeWitness: trackAccount.returnPlate -> trackResolved and poacherFound.askForPayment -> trackResolved bypass compareSaleNote; trackResolved nevertheless states 'the sale terms are compared.'
findings.violatedRule: Outcome narration must not attribute an evidence-review action to routes that did not take it.

findings.defect: The reveal ending claims grain sacks were recovered and the horse freed on routes that only expose/confront the gang or cut its control rope.
findings.routeWitness: stagedBeast.raiseAlarm/cutControlRope/confrontMen(success) -> tollRevealed; none of these choices records sack recovery or horse release, but tollRevealed says the keeper opens the gate after both occurred.
findings.violatedRule: A shared resolution may not promote exposure or interruption into completed recovery of property and an animal.

findings.defect: The physical control-rope cut accepts an owned but BROKEN small knife because it checks inventory presence rather than usability.
findings.routeWitness: stagedBeast.cutControlRope requires smallKnife in items, omits usableItems, damages the knife, and advances to tollRevealed; under the engine's item semantics a BROKEN owned knife still satisfies the presence requirement.
findings.violatedRule: A physically used tool must be usable; possession of broken Gear cannot establish that the action was performed.
findings.implementationEvidence: Physical Gear-use gates at stagedBeast.cutControlRope now require usable condition through usableItems/anyUsableItems. The new CRA-C0004 regression matrix verifies normal Gear remains eligible while BROKEN and absent Gear are rejected for this exact route; see src/craC0004GearUsability.test.ts.

findings.defect: The shared resolution claims the landholder/warden removed the snares and released the animal even after mark-and-withdraw or player-only snare-cut routes; direct tracking also reaches a scene that presumes the landholder arrived.
findings.routeWitness: hideEvidence.followDragMarks -> poacherCamp without askLandholder, yet the scene says the landholder has arrived. poacherCamp.markSnares -> hideResolved does not free the animal or contact a warden; cutSnare(success) frees one animal but neither establishes removal of the second snare nor the landholder/warden actions. hideResolved asserts all outcomes universally.
findings.violatedRule: NPC presence, intervention, and rescue/disposition outcomes require route-specific contact and action proof.

findings.defect: Securing a loose stack with rope reaches a shared ending that says the crew rerouted the cart and the Stoneback stopped shifting stacks, although neither consequence is established by that action.
findings.routeWitness: stonePattern.useRopeStack -> stoneRerouted; the choice secures/damages the rope on one stack but does not move the cart, while stoneRerouted claims upper-bench rerouting and that the Stoneback stops shifting stacks. The distinct rerouteHaul/leaveDenAlone choices actually move work to the upper bench.
findings.violatedRule: A converged outcome must preserve which intervention occurred and may not attribute one branch's results to another action.

findings.defect: After the route tests the hoist with a loose timber, the generated cautious and mishap closures say the Traveler left the hoist untouched.
findings.routeWitness: the-old-hoistEvidence.pressOn -> success to the-old-hoistDecision or failure to the-old-hoistMishap; pressOn is explicitly 'Test the hoist with a loose timber' and failure text says the structure shifts under the work. Both the later cautious ending and mishap append closure 'You leave the hoist untouched.'
findings.violatedRule: A shared closure must preserve prior route actions and object state; an inspected/tested mechanism is not untouched.

findings.defect: The scenario offers taking a loose tool or reaching for a chest, but the generated success endings never state or record either acquisition; after the risky reach's success, the final choice still resolves generically without an object outcome.
findings.routeWitness: camp-below-the-slideEvidence.testGround -> hazardEdge -> advanceFromStable -> Decision -> closeCarefully ('Take only the loose tool') reaches the closure saying the visible edge is recorded; pressOn success -> Decision -> continueSearch ('Reach for the chest') reaches generic bold text with no chest/tool acquisition or disposition. The failed pressOn can be fatal, but the success route remains unresolved.
findings.violatedRule: A consequential salvage choice must resolve the selected object action truthfully; a successful/partial route cannot silently omit whether the object was taken or left.
findings.implementationEvidence: src/scenarios/frontierDiscoveryBatch.ts changes the stable-edge option to inspection-only and gives the successful chest reach an explicit pinned/no-recovery result. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts contrasts inspection, risky success, and fatal failure.

findings.defect: The claim archetype offers a bilateral evidence-sharing action and ending even though this Adventure establishes no claimant or other party to receive the account.
findings.routeWitness: the-hidden-tailings-pileDecision.shareRecord -> the-hidden-tailings-pileCautious; the card's opening/clue/turn describe only the traveler, brush, assay fragments and uncertain purpose/ownership. No claimant is encountered or contacted, yet the generic option says 'Give both sides the same account.'
findings.violatedRule: Choice availability and narrated participation must be supported by people/relationships present in the specific scenario, not supplied by an incompatible generic archetype.
findings.implementationEvidence: The shareRecord archetype is now a private field record for this unclaimed tailings site; its ending explicitly says no claimant was present/contacted. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts covers the selected and private contrast routes.

findings.defect: The generic claim decision offers to give both sides the same account although no claimant or second party is present or contacted in this Adventure.
findings.routeWitness: the-claim-with-no-nameEvidence.readEvidence -> Decision -> shareRecord; all card scenes establish recent work, absent owner markers and an upstream boot track only. The generic bilateral choice has no other party as a valid target, and the cautious result does not narrate communication.
findings.violatedRule: A player option to mediate/share evidence requires identified parties and a route that actually establishes their contact/presence.
findings.implementationEvidence: The absent-claimant route now keeps a private field record and leaves the pan in place; no bilateral report is claimed. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts covers this and the private-record contrast.

findings.defect: The explicitly selected action to take the loose shovel from high ground has no recorded or narrated acquisition outcome; only general hazard insight is granted and later closure does not distinguish shovel taken versus left.
findings.routeWitness: the-washed-out-claimEvidence.testGround -> the-washed-out-claimHazardEdge; testGround is labeled 'Take the loose shovel from high ground' but effects only grant card.insight. advanceFromStable -> Decision -> closeCarefully and retreatFromStable -> Left both use generic closure with no shovel disposition or item gain.
findings.violatedRule: A concrete object-taking action must resolve its custody outcome in route state or narration; a choice cannot promise taking an item while the result leaves acquisition indeterminate.
findings.implementationEvidence: The high-bank option is now inspection-only and the result says the shovel remains in place, not recovered or carried. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts covers the inspection and withdrawal contrast.

findings.defect: The bank-side action to read the bolted ledger-box markings yields no reading or information result on the route; it grants only generic site insight and ends without resolving the promised investigation.
findings.routeWitness: the-old-dredgeEvidence.testGround -> the-old-dredgeHazardEdge; testGround label is 'Read the box markings from the bank' but only grants the general insight. The hazard edge/closure never gives any marking text. The bold pressOn success advances to the same edge without a ledger result, and failure is fatal.
findings.violatedRule: A completed information-gathering action must either deliver the information or clearly state that it could not be obtained; scenario Knowledge/result must match what the route actually investigates.
findings.implementationEvidence: The bank-side marking attempt explicitly resolves as illegible with no ledger contents established; successful boarding reaches a distinct result that leaves the bolted box unopened and unknown. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts covers bank, success, and fatal failure.

findings.defect: The generic bilateral shareRecord action claims both sides receive the same account although only the visitors are present; the employer is represented by a posted map and is never contacted.
findings.routeWitness: claim-jumpers-at-sundownDecision.shareRecord -> Cautious; opening establishes two arriving travelers and an absent employer whose map is posted. No route sends or reports the account to the employer, while the generic choice says 'Give both sides the same account' and adds a shared-evidence history flag.
findings.violatedRule: A narrated bilateral communication or mediation requires a route-established channel to each represented party.
findings.implementationEvidence: The account choice now names only the two present visitors, states the absent employer is not contacted, and records only that one-sided communication. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts verifies recipient and History text.

findings.defect: The generic claim decision offers to give both sides the same account despite no claimant or counterparty being present in this scenario.
findings.routeWitness: the-timber-claimDecision.shareRecord -> Cautious; all card scenes establish cut timber, a leaning unreadable post and drag marks but no person or second claim. The choice records shared evidence and routes to the shared-record ending without identifying or contacting another side.
findings.violatedRule: Bilateral mediation/communication requires established parties and a route that reaches them.
findings.implementationEvidence: The no-claimant timber route now records evidence privately; the result explicitly avoids delivery to another party. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts covers selected and private contrast routes.

findings.defect: The generic claim decision offers to give both sides the same account although no claimant or other party is present or contacted.
findings.routeWitness: the-second-claim-markerDecision.shareRecord -> Cautious; the card establishes only old/new stakes and initials on an undated marker. No claimant appears, yet the generic shareRecord choice describes bilateral evidence-sharing.
findings.violatedRule: Choice availability and narrated participation must be supported by people/relationships present in the specific scenario.
findings.implementationEvidence: The no-claimant boundary route now records both lines privately without claiming bilateral sharing. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts covers selected and private contrast routes.

findings.defect: The generic claim decision implies both sides receive the same account though only the employer is present and no second claimant/recipient is established.
findings.routeWitness: the-claim-that-pays-too-wellDecision.shareRecord -> Cautious; the prospector offers the job in person, while the shed occupant is only inferred from movement and is never identified/contacted. No communication route reaches that occupant, but shareRecord adds a shared-evidence History flag.
findings.violatedRule: A bilateral report requires each party and a delivery/contact route to be established.
findings.implementationEvidence: The account choice now tells only the present prospector; the unseen shed occupant is explicitly not reported to. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts verifies the route and recipient-specific History.

findings.defect: The chosen action to leave a visible note-like marker from the road is never narrated or recorded as completed.
findings.routeWitness: camp-with-fresh-cut-woodEvidence.readEvidence -> Decision and Decision.closeCarefully; both present the cautious action 'Leave a visible note-like marker from the road'. Its effects only grant generic site Knowledge/History, while the ending says the wood and path remain ready and the Traveler did not use the shelter, without saying a marker was left.
findings.violatedRule: A concrete player-selected intervention must be reflected in the resulting scene/state or explicitly left incomplete.
findings.implementationEvidence: The selected visible-marker action now records a factual History flag and its ending acknowledges the marker; the wait route has neither. frontierDiscoveryC0006.test.ts contrasts those outcomes.

findings.defect: Knowledge asserting the couple preferred a brief sincere toast is granted on a route that never asks or hears from the couple.
findings.routeWitness: supper.correctName -> aside.offerWords grants the preference Knowledge. aside says the best man admits mixing up three introductions and that the couple can hear if addressed, but no preference is given; only the separate supper.askCouple route establishes bride/groom preferences.
findings.violatedRule: Knowledge must describe facts actually learned on the selected route, not facts available only on another branch.

findings.defect: The selected 'Accept supper, then explain' route ends after supper without explaining the mistaken identity.
findings.routeWitness: doorstep.acceptMeal -> meal terminal ending. No correction scene is visited; meal says the Traveler shares supper and the host speaks of ordinary things, leaving the mistaken-guest premise unaddressed despite the explicit choice label.
findings.violatedRule: A selected route's promised follow-through must occur or be explicitly declined before the ending.

findings.defect: The shared terminal crossing text credits inspection on routes that never inspect the bridge.
