findings.implementationEvidence: The partial outcome now keeps worker, flock, and wagon states distinct: only movePeople records springWorkersAtRidge; holdGate records only that the flock turned back from the ditch; signaling the wagon crew does not establish they heard or waited. Route-aware variants report those proven facts and keep all other states unconfirmed. Whistle provenance and the coin conclusion no longer call the outcome a full evacuation. wildernessFieldcraftGenreBatch.test.ts covers all three routes and the reward provenance.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Trail Whistle can satisfy a choice that physically uses it to answer the owl call, allowing the route to establish a reply and reunion without functioning signal Gear.
findings.routeWitness: call.answerCall requires items:['trailWhistle'] but omits usableItems. In engine requirement checks, items means inventory membership; only usableItems rejects BROKEN Gear. Trail Whistle is carryable condition-tracked Gear. The answerCall action states ‘Answer with the Trail Whistle and wait’ and routes to reply, where a faint human whistle from the east becomes the basis for the party reuniting or marking the signal point.
findings.violatedRule: Possession is not usability; a physically used Gear item that can be BROKEN must be gated on usable condition before its action/result is available.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Travel Rope can satisfy the choice to anchor a line and reach the bedroll, allowing an unusable rope to enable a physical recovery route.
findings.routeWitness: bedroll.lowerRope -> line -> pullBedroll. lowerRope requires items:['travelRope'] but omits usableItems. The engine accepts inventory inclusion for items and rejects BROKEN condition only through usableItems. Travel Rope is carryable condition-tracked Gear; the line scene then says the rope reaches the bedroll and enables retrieval before owner confirmation.
findings.violatedRule: Physical use of Gear requires usable condition; possession alone cannot establish a safe, functioning anchor or retrieval line.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Signal Flag Set can satisfy the choice to set a visible return marker and establish a flag-guided route.
findings.routeWitness: survey.setFlag -> flag -> returnByFlag. setFlag requires items:['signalFlagSet'] without usableItems. Signal Flag Set is carryable condition-tracked Gear, and the engine’s items check does not reject BROKEN condition; usableItems does. The resulting flag scene asserts a visible red return point from the survey point, enabling the returnByFlag route.
findings.violatedRule: A physical signaling aid must be usable before its route proof or result is established; inventory ownership is not sufficient.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Weatherproof Blanket or Wool Travel Blanket can satisfy the windbreak choice and reach an ending that claims the blanket blocks wind.
findings.routeWitness: log.chooseOverhang -> overhang.secureBlanket -> safe. The choice requires anyItems:['weatherproofBlanket','woolTravelBlanket'] and omits anyUsableItems. Both items are carryable condition-tracked Gear; anyItems checks only inventory inclusion, while anyUsableItems rejects BROKEN Gear. The safe result says the blanket blocks some wind without closing the overhang exits.
findings.violatedRule: An item used as functional protective Gear must be usable; broken inventory must not establish the claimed protection or safe result.

findings.defect: A shared safe ending claims the goods remain together after a route explicitly leaves bedding at the staging shed.
findings.routeWitness: string.leaveBedding sets fourth_mule_bedding_cached -> camp.useBlanket or camp.retreat -> safe. Neither safe route requires fourth_mule_bedding_cached to be recovered; safe unconditionally says ‘the goods remain together.’ The distinct camp.returnBedding choice is the route that returns for the cached bedding.
findings.violatedRule: A converged outcome must preserve route-established object location and custody; a cached load cannot be narrated as together with the party until retrieved.

findings.defect: The scale-only route receives manifest-mark and missing-crate-location information that its selected action does not establish.
findings.routeWitness: manifest.weighSealed (Cargo Balance Scale) -> marks. The route records only crate_weights_checked, but marks asserts the chalk marks were copied from a previous shipment and locates the missing medical crate under the platform ramp. The scale compares the sealed loads; this route does not compare waybill marks or search the siding. checkWaybill and searchSiding are the separate branches that can establish those discoveries.
findings.violatedRule: A route may not gain specific information or location knowledge at convergence unless the selected action or subsequent scene establishes how it was learned.

findings.defect: The shared partial outcome claims both food and water arrive after a route that explicitly carries only water.
findings.routeWitness: wheel.secureWheel -> repair.abandon (label: ‘Leave the wagon and carry only the water’) -> partial. The terminal text unconditionally says ‘The crew receives water and food.’ The separate wheel.takeWater route explicitly carries both water and food and reaches the same ending; no route state distinguishes the delivered supplies.
findings.violatedRule: Shared outcome narration must retain route-specific cargo and delivery state; a route that carries only one supply cannot inherit the other supply’s arrival.

findings.defect: The shared finish claims all three camp tasks are complete on successful routes that resolve only the selected task and one follow-up, leaving another task without route proof.
findings.routeWitness: board.stoveFirst -> cook.record -> finish records only the task order and delay after the stove task was selected; no bridge-brace or survey-chain completion is established. Similarly, bridgeFirst -> bridge.borrow resolves the stove alternative but does not establish the survey-chain check, while measureFirst -> survey.correct does not establish completion of the cook’s stove task. finish unconditionally says all three tasks are completed before the next shift.
findings.violatedRule: A shared completion result may claim only tasks/outcomes established by the selected route or explicit intervening resolution.

findings.defect: The secure-only crate route reaches a scene that asserts the Traveler found the crew above the cut without following the location clue.
findings.routeWitness: camp.secureCrate sets resupply_crate_sheltered and enters tracks; tracks says ‘The Crew Is Above the Cut’ and identifies two workers checking the washout. Only camp.followPrint records following the uphill print to locate the crew; the secure-only route establishes no person/location discovery.
findings.violatedRule: A converged scene may not assert discovery of a person or their location unless the selected route establishes how they were found.

findings.defect: The braced-cart route reaches a result claiming the timber arrives later even though that route never leaves or caches the timber.
findings.routeWitness: cart.braceHandle sets handcart_braced -> cut.protectOil -> paid. No choice on this path sets handcart_wedges_left or otherwise unloads/caches the timber, but paid says the mine crew receives food and lamp oil while timber arrives later. The separate cart.reduceLoad -> cut.deliverEssentials path explicitly leaves wedges and supports the split-delivery result.
findings.violatedRule: Shared delivery narration must preserve route-established cargo custody and destination; delayed cargo requires an explicit unload/cache/second-trip state.

findings.defect: The sealed-message/signal route can receive settlement credit for securing working records although it never secures the survey books.
findings.routeWitness: office.leaveMessage -> signal.waitCrew -> paid. leaveMessage sets office_signal_set and leaves the envelope sealed; it does not set office_books_secured. The paid scene offers a Lockable Map Case or coins ‘for securing the working records.’
findings.violatedRule: A reward justification or converged result may credit only route actions actually established; protecting the message does not establish securing the books.

findings.defect: Anchor-inspection/manual-comparison routes converge on text claiming gauge readings and a repeat they did not perform.
findings.routeWitness: brief.readAnchor -> reading asserts the gauge shows unequal strain despite the choice being inspection before any pull; reading.compareByHand -> result then claims a consistent low repeat although the selected follow-up compares by hand with the block grounded. lowTest -> stopAndReset is the route that establishes the low gauge repeat.
findings.violatedRule: Instrument readings and test completion may be narrated only when the route performed the measurement under the stated conditions.

findings.defect: Inspection-only route inherits pad-fit and successful-walk claims without ever fitting the pad.
findings.routeWitness: yard.inspectGirth -> trail says the pad spreads pressure and saddle turns on the rise; trail.replaceGirth -> result says the pad stays centered on a careful walk. That route inspects/replaces the girth but does not choose yard.fitPad. The fitPad route alone establishes the pad’s use during the walk.
findings.violatedRule: A shared scene and result must not claim a route-specific equipment intervention or its outcome when that intervention was not selected.

findings.defect: The upper-only measurement route receives a two-site rainfall comparison and completion credit for recording both sites.
findings.routeWitness: cup.upperOnly -> result asserts the pasture cup shows more rain than the mill yard without a yard reading; result.compareGround -> offer still claims both sites were recorded and the tributary marked. The placeBoth route plus mapRunoff establishes the comparison and record; upperOnly does not.
findings.violatedRule: A measurement comparison or reward claim requires every referenced measurement/site and follow-up action to have been established on that route.
findings.implementationEvidence: The upperOnly choice now enters an explicit one-site reading scene. A second mill-yard placement is required before the two-site comparison/result; choosing to stop receives neutral single-reading text. Regression drives upper-only, stop, second-site placement, and the original placeBoth route. Equipment Testing suite passes 16 tests.

findings.defect: Rim inspection alone converges on an asserted spare-wheel key fit and soft-tooth test result that was never measured.
findings.routeWitness: wheel.inspectRim -> result says the altered key fits the spare nipple and has a bright burr showing a soft tooth; inspectRim checks the rim only and records no key test. wheel.testSpare is the route that establishes fit and tooth failure.
findings.violatedRule: Test results and instrument/tool findings may not be asserted on a route that did not perform the test.
findings.implementationEvidence: Rim-only inspection now enters a distinct scene that either performs the unloaded spare-spoke test or ends with neutral unverified text. Tests confirm the actual testSpare route and test-after-inspection route retain the fit/burr findings, while inspection/defer does not. Equipment Testing suite passes 17 tests.

findings.defect: Vent-only inspection inherits leeward flame and hinge-orientation test results without lighting/testing the lamp on that side.
findings.routeWitness: lamp.checkVent -> signal asserts the screen steadies the flame on the leeward side and the hinge directs light away. The checkVent route only inspects the top vent; lamp.testLeeward establishes the flame behavior and lamp orientation test.
findings.violatedRule: A shared test-result scene must retain which physical test was performed and may not attribute an unperformed test to an inspection-only route.

findings.defect: The decline-upgrade branch receives unconditional narration that the strap gained its persistent upgrade.
findings.routeWitness: strap.inspectSeam -> test states the strap gains stitchedBuckle before offering accept or stop. accept applies upgrade('freightmansStrap','stitchedBuckle'); stop only sets declined_freightmans_strap_upgrade, yet both reach done saying the actual condition and upgrade are recorded.
findings.violatedRule: Persistent item upgrades and their completion narration must follow the selected acceptance/effect path; declining must not be represented as upgraded.

findings.defect: A straight-edge reference check converges on a diagnosis that claims an end-for-end reversal test was performed and proved the vial off-center.
findings.routeWitness: level.checkPlank -> diagnosis asserts the bubble reverses on the same plank and the vial is off-center. Only level.reverseLevel performs the same-plank reversal; checkPlank compares the plank to a straight edge.
findings.violatedRule: A diagnosis may not claim a test result or causal conclusion not established by the selected route.

findings.defect: Seam-only inspection converges on a claim that the scale confirmed the sack weight difference.
findings.routeWitness: scale.inspectSeam -> seam says the scale confirms a difference; inspectSeam only inspects the tied seam. compareSacks is the route that weighs both sacks and records the difference.
findings.violatedRule: A measurement result may only be asserted when that measurement was performed on the route.

findings.defect: Using an existing Lantern Guard converges on text saying the prototype cage hinge was tightened and tested.
findings.routeWitness: lamp.useExisting -> rut says ‘After the hinge is tightened’ and credits the cage with a clear-glass short dry run. useExisting only fits the separate Lantern Guard and compares; only lamp.tightHinge tightens the prototype hinge.
findings.violatedRule: A shared route result must not credit a different intervention than the one selected.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Folding Bench Clamp passes an ownership-only gate for physically holding the press guide and can establish the proof result.
findings.routeWitness: press.markPath requires items:['foldingBenchClamp'] but omits usableItems; engine requirement semantics reject BROKEN condition only through usableItems. The Folding Bench Clamp is carryable condition-tracked GEAR. The choice then enters proof, which claims the guide stayed in place during a slow proof.
findings.violatedRule: A physical Gear-use action must require usable condition; ownership alone cannot prove a broken tool performed its function.
findings.implementationEvidence: Physical Gear-use gates at press.markPath now require usable condition through usableItems/anyUsableItems. The new CRA-C0004 regression matrix verifies normal Gear remains eligible while BROKEN and absent Gear are rejected for this exact route; see src/craC0004GearUsability.test.ts.

findings.defect: Known-weight comparison converges on a narrative that says the gauge’s zero was checked and found dusty.
findings.routeWitness: spring.compareWeights -> calibrate unconditionally says ‘The zero check confirms dust at the pivot’; compareWeights compares two loads and does not check zero. zeroGauge is the route that establishes the zero-check result.
findings.violatedRule: A shared diagnosis may not claim an inspection or test step that the route did not perform.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Boat Hook passes an ownership-only gate for retrieving a crate and can establish intact recovery/custody.
findings.routeWitness: dock.boatHook requires items:['boatHook'] without usableItems. Boat Hook is carryable condition-tracked GEAR; engine items checks do not reject BROKEN condition. The route enters caught, which says the crate was brought against the landing without breaking its seal.
findings.violatedRule: A physical retrieval tool must be usable before its route result can claim successful recovery.
findings.implementationEvidence: Physical Gear-use gates at dock.boatHook now require usable condition through usableItems/anyUsableItems. The new CRA-C0004 regression matrix verifies normal Gear remains eligible while BROKEN and absent Gear are rejected for this exact route; see src/craC0004GearUsability.test.ts.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Collapsible Sounding Rod passes an ownership-only gate for probing the ford and can establish the sounding route result.
findings.routeWitness: ford.probe requires items:['collapsibleSoundingRod'] but omits usableItems. engine.meets checks only inventory presence for items; condition-tracked BROKEN Gear is excluded only by usableItems. The route reaches channel and its downstream shallow-shelf finding.
findings.violatedRule: Physical use of condition-tracked Gear requires usable condition; ownership alone cannot establish an instrument result.
findings.implementationEvidence: Physical Gear-use gates at ford.probe now require usable condition through usableItems/anyUsableItems. The new CRA-C0004 regression matrix verifies normal Gear remains eligible while BROKEN and absent Gear are rejected for this exact route; see src/craC0004GearUsability.test.ts.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Travel Rope passes an ownership-only gate for setting the second shore line and can establish the secured-barge result.
findings.routeWitness: barge.rope requires items:['travelRope'] without usableItems; BROKEN condition is not excluded by items. It enters line, which states the second line is set and the stern no longer reaches the lighter.
findings.violatedRule: A physical Gear-use action must require usable condition before its successful result is available.
findings.implementationEvidence: Physical Gear-use gates at barge.rope now require usable condition through usableItems/anyUsableItems. The new CRA-C0004 regression matrix verifies normal Gear remains eligible while BROKEN and absent Gear are rejected for this exact route; see src/craC0004GearUsability.test.ts.

findings.defect: Moving the lighter clear converges on text claiming a second shore line was set and the chafe point protected.
findings.routeWitness: barge.move -> line; move clears the lighter only. line says 'With the second line set' and kept says unloading resumes only after the rub point is protected. Only barge.rope establishes a second line.
findings.violatedRule: Converged results must preserve which route action occurred and may not claim an unperformed securing action.

findings.defect: BROKEN signal flags or a BROKEN roadside signal mirror pass ownership-only gates and can reach a result claiming the boat held for a signal.
findings.routeWitness: lamp.flags requires items:['signalFlagSet'] and lamp.mirror requires items:['roadsideSignalMirror']; neither requires usableItems. Engine condition semantics allow BROKEN possession through items-only gates, while signal says the boat stopped and paid says the closure sign was acknowledged.
findings.violatedRule: A physical signaling tool must be usable before its route can establish that the signal was sent or acknowledged.
findings.implementationEvidence: Physical Gear-use gates at lamp.flags/mirror now require usable condition through usableItems/anyUsableItems. The new CRA-C0004 regression matrix verifies normal Gear remains eligible while BROKEN and absent Gear are rejected for this exact route; see src/craC0004GearUsability.test.ts.

findings.defect: The Boat Hook branch reaches shared narration that says the far-bank operator answered despite no signal being sent.
findings.routeWitness: ferry.hook -> slack; hook says use the Boat Hook to move the branch, while only ferry.signal sends a signal. slack unconditionally says the far operator answers and the current relaxes.
findings.violatedRule: A shared route result may not invent an NPC response or communication event absent from the chosen route.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Collapsible Sounding Rod passes an ownership-only gate for probing and can reach the specific timber-location result.
findings.routeWitness: bridge.probe requires items:['collapsibleSoundingRod'] without usableItems. BROKEN condition still satisfies items; the route reaches hazard, claiming a broken timber below the near arch.
findings.violatedRule: Physical use of condition-tracked Gear requires usable condition before it can establish a result.
findings.implementationEvidence: Physical Gear-use gates at bridge.probe now require usable condition through usableItems/anyUsableItems. The new CRA-C0004 regression matrix verifies normal Gear remains eligible while BROKEN and absent Gear are rejected for this exact route; see src/craC0004GearUsability.test.ts.

findings.defect: An old-pier water-level comparison converges on a specific submerged-timber finding that the comparison does not establish.
findings.routeWitness: bridge.mark -> hazard; mark only compares the current level to an old pier depth mark. hazard asserts a broken timber below the near arch, visible when current slackens. The opening punt bump establishes an obstruction generally, not its specific material/location or slack-current sighting.
findings.violatedRule: A finding or diagnosis may not claim a specific observation/location beyond the evidence established on that route.

findings.defect: The replace/tag-out route converges on a tactile splice-test result that only the inspection route establishes.
findings.routeWitness: rope.replace -> paid -> choice; replace tags the line out and brings a spare without flexing the splice. choice says the stiff fibers catch at the splice, which is established by rope.inspect. Initial visible pale/stiff fibers do not establish catching under flex.
findings.violatedRule: Converged scene text must not claim a test or tactile result not performed on the selected route.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Collapsible Sounding Rod passes an ownership-only gate for sounding the channel and can establish the deeper-run result.

clusters.name: Route-specific state lost at convergence
clusters.description: Route-specific location, outcome, person/helper, object, method, or prior-intervention facts are lost at convergence, causing shared scenes/endings to assert facts not established by every incoming route.

clusters.name: Knowledge/History without route proof
clusters.description: Knowledge and/or History is granted without sufficient route proof that the Traveler actually learned or established it.

clusters.name: Elapsed-time proxy used as event proof
clusters.description: Elapsed time is used as a proxy for a specific event/consequence, making later narration claim that event on routes where it did not occur.

clusters.name: Gear ownership treated as Gear usability
clusters.description: Choices that physically use Gear check only that it remains in inventory, allowing BROKEN gear to satisfy the action requirement instead of requiring usableItems.

clusters.name: A single fee can be refunded more than once
clusters.description: A payment is refunded by an intermediate choice effect and then refunded again by a follow-up refund choice, producing net compensation beyond the paid amount.

clusters.name: Generic frontier archetypes promise unsupported actors or action outcomes
clusters.description: The shared Frontier Discovery builder applies archetype-level choices/results without adapting them to the card's established people or route effects, so a choice can promise absent-party communication or a concrete object action that the route never resolves.

clusters.name: NPC consensus inferred from a unilateral route choice
clusters.description: A player-selected record or action is persisted as a group agreement or collective authorship even though the affected NPCs were not asked to participate or consent.

clusters.name: Equipment-specific action without availability gate
clusters.description: A route offers a concrete action whose authored method names carryable Gear without checking that the Traveler possesses and can use that Gear, and without establishing another in-scene source.

clusters.name: Granted Gear condition disagrees with route-established condition
clusters.description: A Gear reward’s authored condition is not preserved mechanically: an explicitly frayed/damaged item may default to NORMAL, or a sound spare may be granted as DAMAGED because an unrelated repair marker is applied to it.

clusters.name: Post-action complication disclosed before its trigger
clusters.description: A shared industrial-work builder inserts later complication/test outcomes into the diagnosis scene before repair, shutdown, or rush is chosen, making future events appear already established and sometimes contradicting the pre-action diagnosis.

clusters.name: Method result disclosed before method choice
clusters.description: The shared construction builder inserts a result produced by a measurement or tool action into the preceding work scene, so inspection and rush routes receive findings they did not establish.

clusters.name: Choice-promised follow-through omitted before termination
clusters.description: A route explicitly promises a follow-up action, but reaches a terminal outcome without performing or explicitly declining that action, leaving the selected intent unresolved.

clusters.title: Route-specific state lost at convergence
clusters.definition: Route-specific location, outcome, person/helper, object, method, or prior-intervention facts are lost at convergence, causing shared scenes/endings to assert facts not established by every incoming route.
clusters.repairLayer: Primarily scenario-specific route gates, shared-ending variants, or narrow run-local proof; broad cross-family pattern.
clusters.expectedRepairReach: Very large; 212 live Adventures and 222 assignments.
clusters.regressionRisk: High: repairs can affect shared endings, rescue/outcome claims, and reward eligibility.
clusters.validation: Finding-by-finding route matrix; assert both positive and absent-proof routes, including save/resume where stateful.

clusters.title: Knowledge/History without route proof
clusters.definition: Knowledge and/or History is granted without sufficient route proof that the Traveler actually learned or established it.
clusters.repairLayer: Scenario-local Knowledge/History award gates; selectively shared persistence helpers.
clusters.regressionRisk: High for persistent save data and durable facts.
clusters.validation: Knowledge/History acquisition route tests plus save/reload and negative-route checks.

clusters.title: Elapsed-time proxy used as event proof
clusters.definition: Elapsed time is used as a proxy for a specific event/consequence, making later narration claim that event on routes where it did not occur.
clusters.validation: Test elapsed-time route without event versus event-established route.

clusters.title: Gear ownership treated as Gear usability
clusters.definition: Choices that physically use Gear check only that it remains in inventory, allowing BROKEN gear to satisfy the action requirement instead of requiring usableItems.
clusters.repairLayer: Scenario choice requirements (`usableItems`) or a narrow Gear usability helper if callers prove uniform semantics.
clusters.regressionRisk: High for broken Gear routes and route availability.
clusters.validation: Test NORMAL/DAMAGED/BROKEN Gear and no-Gear alternatives per affected route.

clusters.title: A single fee can be refunded more than once
clusters.definition: A payment is refunded by an intermediate choice effect and then refunded again by a follow-up refund choice, producing net compensation beyond the paid amount.
clusters.repairLayer: Scenario-specific compensation accounting; potentially one-shot refund token.
clusters.validation: Assert paid amount, refund effect count, and final balance for every follow-up.

clusters.title: Generic frontier archetypes promise unsupported actors or action outcomes
clusters.definition: The shared Frontier Discovery builder applies archetype-level choices/results without adapting them to the card's established people or route effects, so a choice can promise absent-party communication or a concrete object action that the route never resolves.
clusters.repairLayer: Shared Frontier Discovery builder, with per-card data correction where appropriate.
clusters.expectedRepairReach: Moderate/high; 17 assignments across 15 Adventures in one builder.
clusters.regressionRisk: High because one template change can affect all generated cards.
clusters.validation: Enumerate every builder caller and snapshot each route’s actors, promises, and resolved action outcome.

clusters.title: NPC consensus inferred from a unilateral route choice
clusters.definition: A player-selected record or action is persisted as a group agreement or collective authorship even though the affected NPCs were not asked to participate or consent.
clusters.repairLayer: Scenario-specific consent/participant gating and persistent group-credit wording.
clusters.validation: Test unilateral choice versus explicit participant consent and persisted record.

clusters.title: Equipment-specific action without availability gate
clusters.definition: A route offers a concrete action whose authored method names carryable Gear without checking that the Traveler possesses and can use that Gear, and without establishing another in-scene source.
clusters.repairLayer: Choice-level inventory/usability requirements or explicit in-scene source for the tool.
clusters.expectedRepairReach: Moderate; 12 Adventures, mostly investigation builder callers.
clusters.regressionRisk: Moderate; can remove routes for fresh Travelers if fallback omitted.
clusters.validation: Test Gear present/usable, absent, and unusable plus a truthful fallback.

clusters.title: Granted Gear condition disagrees with route-established condition
clusters.definition: A Gear reward’s authored condition is not preserved mechanically: an explicitly frayed/damaged item may default to NORMAL, or a sound spare may be granted as DAMAGED because an unrelated repair marker is applied to it.
clusters.repairLayer: Reward item condition/provenance effects at the scenario grant site.
clusters.validation: Assert item condition and provenance before/after save/reload for each reward route.

clusters.title: Post-action complication disclosed before its trigger
clusters.definition: A shared industrial-work builder inserts later complication/test outcomes into the diagnosis scene before repair, shutdown, or rush is chosen, making future events appear already established and sometimes contradicting the pre-action diagnosis.
clusters.repairLayer: Shared industrial mill/rail builder scene ordering.
clusters.regressionRisk: Moderate/high due template fanout and safety complication timing.
clusters.validation: For every builder story compare diagnosis before action with post-action complication after each trigger.

clusters.title: Method result disclosed before method choice
clusters.definition: The shared construction builder inserts a result produced by a measurement or tool action into the preceding work scene, so inspection and rush routes receive findings they did not establish.
clusters.regressionRisk: High because method-result placement affects all stories and some Gear gates.
clusters.validation: For every story, inspect/rush must not receive measurement result; measure/tool route must receive it afterward.

clusters.title: Choice-promised follow-through omitted before termination
clusters.definition: A route explicitly promises a follow-up action, but reaches a terminal outcome without performing or explicitly declining that action, leaving the selected intent unresolved.
clusters.repairLayer: Scenario-local route continuation or terminal result; preserve the selected follow-through intent.
clusters.regressionRisk: Low-to-moderate; local choice-flow change with possible ending text effects.
clusters.validation: Test the promised-follow-through route and a contrasting route that explicitly defers or declines correction.

highSeverityFindings.defect: Withdrawal from an active drowning emergency converges on a neutral recreation ending that erases the unresolved swimmer emergency.
Shared closure attributes an anonymous threat to the tailor and records that culpability as Knowledge on paths that never establish the tailor's role or intent.
The boundary-disturbance escape/combat route converges on an ending that says the missing tenant is out when that route never found or rescued him.
The shared ending claims a mason capped the well and discovered its speaking tube on departure/retreat routes that never summon or consult the mason.
Shared closure declares the missing-body cause known and assigns a family disposition after bypass routes never find the living cooper.
Calling the driver to abandon the wagon is treated as proof that he reached shore, producing a rescue claim without a completed crossing.
Unwarned routes converge on an ending that says workers were counted outside although their evacuation was never established.
The rope rescue action accepts a BROKEN travel rope because it checks inventory presence rather than usability, then records a successful miner rescue and History credit.
Fetching the keeper from outside the cellar reaches a rescue ending that says the seller reached the yard and the keeper boarded the service opening, without establishing either action.
Comparing the Red Door Token after opening the lower seal exits through text falsely claiming the door was restored.
A direct climb-to-top success can reach the safe lower-ledge result and prize without establishing avoidance of the expressly excluded cracked upper shelf.
The direct sling-start route can receive the safe-anchor finish and prize without establishing that the cracked nearest ring was avoided in favor of the sound beam.
The shared flood-safe partial outcome claims that workers are on the ridge and the flock is gathered above flood when several incoming routes establish neither or only one of those outcomes.

repairWaves.focus: High-severity route/outcome truth and Gear usability; verify dependencies before batching.
Shared family builders and equipment-gated action templates.
Knowledge/History provenance, reward condition/provenance, and NPC consent/persistent group credit.
Isolated time/event proof and one-time compensation accounting; can be handled as small local repairs.
Remaining medium/low scenario-specific convergence defects after the shared/high-risk first slice.

recommendedFirstRepairTarget.reason: It carries 12 of 13 known HIGH findings and affects 212 live Adventures (222 assignments), making unsupported rescue/person/outcome claims the broadest player-facing correctness risk. Start verification-first, then repair the highest-severity local instances; do not mistake broad cluster membership for one safe global code edit.
recommendedFirstRepairTarget.validation: Route truth matrices for every selected finding; paired positive/negative outcome regressions; save/reload for persistent state; rerun adjacent healthy routes and reward/withdrawal cases.

authoringRuleRecommendations.safeguard: In generated builders, keep measurement and post-action result fields out of scenes reachable before their establishing action; add a template test that inspects every story variant.
For every convergence, enumerate incoming route facts and explicitly test meaningful non-occurrence (not found, not moved, not handed off, not completed) with neutral fallback text.
Every persistent Knowledge/History grant must name the route action and evidence that teaches it; test a nearby route that does not perform that action.
For physical Gear actions and rewards, validate ownership, usable condition, source/provenance, and granted condition separately; preserve a fresh-Traveler fallback.
Do not persist group agreement, consent, or collective authorship from one Traveler-selected action without the affected participants’ explicit assent.
Model refunds as one-time compensation events and test total paid/refunded balance across every reachable follow-up.
